## AINews

**Priority: HIGH**

### Top Updates
* SpaceXAI (formerly xAI) released **Grok 4.6**, a major update to their flagship model, which is positioned as a frontier-level agentic model for coding, knowledge work, and long-running tasks. The model has a **500,000-token context window**, supports text and image inputs, and is available in Cursor, Grok Build, and through API/infrastructure partners.
* **Grok 4.6** is trained on a wide range of agentic RL tasks, including knowledge work, general coding, and domain-specific environments such as kernel optimization, web development, and computer-aided design. The model is described as a major step up from **Grok 4.5** at the same price.
* The release of **Grok 4.6** is significant because it intensifies competition in agentic coding and knowledge-work workflows, where models are increasingly judged on sustained multi-step performance and tool use rather than single-turn answers.
* **Grok 4.6** is available at a pricing starting at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, which is materially below frontier peers.
* Independent evaluations from **Artificial Analysis** place **Grok 4.6** at **61 on the Intelligence Index**, roughly in line with **GPT-5.6 Sol Max**, behind **Claude Opus/Fable**, with strong agentic results including **88.4% on Terminal-Bench v2.1**, **1753 GDPval-AA v2 Elo**, and competitive **AA-Briefcase** performance at far lower cost.
* **Elon Musk** announced that **Grok 4.7** is already in flight, with initial training complete and supplemental training on SpaceX internal data planned.
* Other notable updates include the release of **Qwen3.8-Max** open weights, **DeepSeek V4 Pro GA**, and **Microsoft's MAI-Thinking-1** model.
* The newsletter also covers various other topics, including open-weight multimodal and edge models, inference, compression, and systems, as well as agents, harnesses, and developer tooling.

### Notable Links
* Grok 4.6
* Qwen3.8-Max

## Anna's Daybreak News

**Priority: MEDIUM**

* Karoline Leavitt, the youngest White House press secretary in U.S. history, will leave her position by the end of August to become one of President Trump's top outside advisers and help the Republican Party in the November midterms.
* Trump and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi plan to mine rare earths near Minamitorishima, about 1,000 miles southeast of Tokyo, despite extreme technical and cost barriers.

additionalContext.context:
Grok 4.6 is the latest flagship model from SpaceXAI (formerly xAI), released on August 12, 2026, and positioned around **long-running agents**, coding, knowledge work, and more ambitious interactive/visual tasks. The company says it is designed to stay on complex tasks across many steps—such as researching, analyzing information, working in codebases, and turning ideas into applications or work artifacts—and that it was trained with expanded agentic reinforcement learning across coding, web development, CAD, kernel optimization, and related environments.[1][2][5]

The release matters because SpaceXAI is pitching Grok 4.6 as a frontier-level agentic model rather than just a chat model: it reportedly matches GPT-5.6 Sol on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and improves over Grok 4.5 across several coding and agent benchmarks. It is already available in Cursor, Grok Build, and through API/infrastructure partners, with pricing starting at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens; the broader industry impact is that this intensifies competition in agentic coding and knowledge-work workflows, where models are increasingly judged on sustained multi-step performance and tool use rather than single-turn answers.[1][2][3][4]

SpaceXAI appears to be a misspelling or variant naming of xAI in the AI/ML context; the official product materials describe the company’s latest flagship model, **Grok 4.6**, as its frontier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work.[4][5][6] The model has a **500,000-token context window**, supports text and image inputs, and is positioned for long-running agents that can stay on complex tasks across many steps, including research, codebase analysis, and building polished applications.[2][4][6]

The latest development is the launch of Grok 4.6 on August 12, 2026, following Grok 4.5, with xAI saying it uses a longer supplemental training run, curated model-generated reasoning data, high-quality engineering data, and broader agentic RL training across environments such as kernel optimization, web development, and CAD.[1][6] xAI says Grok 4.6 is available in Cursor, Grok Build, the API, and partner platforms like OpenRouter, Vercel, and Cloudflare, with pricing starting at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens; this matters because it signals continued competition in frontier agentic models aimed at enterprise and developer workflows rather than only chat benchmarks.[5][6]

AI Automation Society appears to be a community-oriented AI automation group with an online presence on Skool and its own site, branded around helping members “learn it,” “use it,” and “scale it.”[1][5] Based on the available results, it is best understood as a practitioner and business-focused network centered on AI automation rather than a formal standards body or professional society like ISA or IEEE.[1][2][8]

The most relevant recent context is that the broader AI/automation market is shifting toward *agentic AI*, governance, and industrial use cases, which gives groups like AI Automation Society practical relevance for operators, founders, and automation builders.[3][2] While the search results do not show major standalone press coverage about this specific group, its newsletter and posts suggest it is tracking AI business developments and translating them into community learning and applied automation workflows, which matters because demand for automation is broadening across industries and AI-related operational risk is becoming a major topic.[3][6]

“Chase AI Community” appears to be a Skool-based community tied to the Chase AI brand rather than JPMorgan Chase’s corporate AI program. The public presence is limited, but the available web listings suggest it is an online group/community focused on helping members “turn AI into [their] unfair advantage,” which points to education, networking, and practical AI/ML use cases rather than a formal research lab or product organization.[1][2] A third-party review also refers to a related “Chase AI+” community, reinforcing that this is likely a creator-led or membership-based AI community with an active online footprint.[3]

Skool is primarily a **community platform** for paid groups, courses, and member engagement, rather than a dedicated AI/ML company. In the AI space, it is being used to host communities such as **AI Automation Society** and **AI Lab**, which shows that Skool has become a practical home for creator-led AI education and monetization communities.[1][7] Its core appeal is the all-in-one structure: community, content, payments, and engagement tools in one place, which lowers friction for AI educators and operators compared with stitching together multiple tools.[6][10]

The latest relevant signal is that AI-focused communities are actively forming and growing on Skool, suggesting it matters most as an **infrastructure layer for AI learning and business-building communities** rather than as a model builder or research platform.[1][7] Industry impact is indirect but real: Skool helps non-technical founders, coaches, and practitioners package AI knowledge into paid communities and training products, which supports the broader commercialization of AI skills. Public third-party coverage also describes Skool as a simple, flat-fee community platform with gamified engagement, reinforcing why it is attractive for AI creators scaling membership-based businesses.[10]

missingStories.headline: EU AI Act enforcement goes live across Europe
missingStories.summary: The European Union’s AI Act crossed from statute book into daily enforcement on August 2, 2026. Companies operating in Europe must disclose when users are interacting with AI, mark generative outputs in machine-readable form, and disclose deepfakes or AI-written public-interest content; the Commission also gained enforcement powers over general-purpose models.[1]
missingStories.whyItMatters: This is a major compliance shift for any AI product touching the EU market. Practitioners need to update disclosure, provenance, and governance workflows immediately to avoid regulatory risk.[1]
missingStories.source: ETC Journal reporting on the EU AI Act

missingStories.headline: DeepSeek V4 Pro launches in general availability
missingStories.summary: DeepSeek reportedly released the general-availability version of its V4 Pro model on August 13, 2026. The release is being framed as one of the day’s major open-model announcements from China.[5]
missingStories.whyItMatters: A new frontier model release from a major Chinese lab can shift the open-weight and low-cost model landscape quickly. Teams tracking model selection, cost, and benchmark performance will want to evaluate it for production use.[5]

missingStories.headline: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-2.4T open-weight MoE model
missingStories.summary: Alibaba’s Qwen team reportedly launched Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, described as a 2.4 trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 95 billion active parameters per token. The release is presented as a major open-weight model event for the day.[5]
missingStories.whyItMatters: Large MoE releases matter because they can deliver frontier-level capability with lower inference cost than dense models. Practitioners following open-source and self-hosted deployments will care about architecture, licensing, and serving efficiency.[5]

missingStories.headline: Researchers report a method for stealing reasoning traces from proprietary LLM APIs
missingStories.summary: A paper from researchers affiliated with the ELLIS Institute Tübingen, Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems, MATS, and Snyk reportedly demonstrates that proprietary LLM reasoning traces can be extracted. The finding is being discussed as a serious vulnerability for closed-model providers.[5]
missingStories.whyItMatters: If reasoning traces can be recovered, model providers may need to redesign API defenses and logging policies. For practitioners, this affects model security, prompt confidentiality, and the trust assumptions behind chain-of-thought style systems.[5]

missingStories.headline: Anthropic hires Andrej Karpathy to strengthen pretraining research
missingStories.summary: Andrej Karpathy reportedly joined Anthropic to rebuild its pretraining research team. The move was previously highlighted in AI news coverage as a notable talent acquisition in 2026.[4]
missingStories.whyItMatters: Leadership hires of this scale often signal strategic investment in frontier model training and research direction. Teams watching the competitive landscape should track how this changes Anthropic’s model roadmap and research velocity.[4]
